findings.claim: The machine-specific path verifier only rejects macOS `/Users/...` and Windows `C:\Users\...` paths, so Linux home-directory absolute Flint paths can still pass default-CI evidence.
findings.evidence: The plan acceptance requires "Default CI contains no machine-specific paths," but `assertNoMachineSpecificPaths` only tests `/\/Users\/[^/]+\//` and `/[A-Za-z]:\\Users\\[^\\]+\\/`, missing common absolute developer paths such as `/home/alice/.../flint-realtime-fabric`.
findings.suggested_fix: Reject absolute home/workstation paths across supported environments, e.g. `/\/home\/[^/]+\//`, `/\/Users\/[^/]+\//`, Windows user profiles, and absolute Flint sibling repository paths, or use a stricter rule that forbids absolute paths to external Flint roots in default-CI files.

findings.claim: The client-secret scan still silently skips whole example subtrees such as `build`, `dist`, `.next`, and `target` instead of classifying all text-like example files.
findings.evidence: The blocking `security-and-secret-boundaries` constraint requires service-role credential boundaries across all text-like example files, but `ignoredDirectories` includes `".next"`, `"build"`, `"dist"`, `"node_modules"`, and `"target"`, and `collectFiles` omits those directories entirely before `readTextLikeFile` can classify text versus binary.
findings.suggested_fix: Do not globally skip example subtrees when making an "all text-like example files" claim; traverse them and classify binary/generated files explicitly, or narrow the documented claim and acceptance evidence to the checked source/config subset.
